documents.unit: Office of Academic Integrity, Undergraduate Education
documents.title: Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The page says instructors "are encouraged to consider" practices and to "Include your specific guidelines in course syllabi", leaving permission to each instructor; it only notes unauthorized use "could be considered a violation". It sets no default ban or permission, so delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty-facing integrity guidance that sets no university-wide AI rule. It advises instructors to learn the tools, state their own expectations in syllabi, design assignments around AI, require citation if AI is allowed, and treat unauthorized use as a possible integrity violation without relying on detectors.

units.why: The page says AI tools can be used "in a productive, creative, and educational manner" or to cheat; this is a statement of principle and sets no rule, so it is general/informs and fits the framework type P56 rather than a stance type.
units.anchor: AI tools may be used in a productive, creative, and educational manner
units.frag_start: AI tools may be used in
units.policy: AI tools may be used in a productive, creative, and educational manner, or they can be used to cheat, plagiarize, or attempt to disguise plagiarism.

units.why: The passage says unauthorized use "could be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy", classing unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36); it is addressed to everyone as a fact, so informs.
units.anchor: could be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy
units.policy: Unauthorized use of such tools could be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy.

units.why: Instructors are told to "Learn how ChatGPT and other tools ... work. Use them yourself", which is support for faculty learning about AI before setting course policy (P63).
units.anchor: Learn how ChatGPT and other tools
units.policy: Instructors learn how ChatGPT and other tools work and use them themselves.

units.why: "Think about how the tools might be used creatively in your course" with demonstration, critique and information-literacy uses asks instructors to teach or demonstrate AI use, fitting P44.
units.anchor: Think about how the tools might be used creatively in your course.
units.policy: Instructors think about how AI tools might be used creatively in the course, to demonstrate pros and cons, view with an information literacy lens, and analyze and critique what the generators produce.

units.why: "Follow best practices in creating assignments that minimize the opportunity to use AI tools" is assignment redesign around AI (P35), conditioned on the instructor not wanting students to use them.
units.anchor: creating assignments that minimize the opportunity to use AI tools or use them successfully
units.frag_end: (if you do not want students using them).
units.policy: Instructors who do not want students using AI tools follow best practices in creating assignments that minimize the opportunity to use AI tools or use them successfully.

units.why: "require citations as you would for any source" when allowing text-generating tools sets a citation expectation (P24); the human-source analogy (P45) is only a comparison, so P24 fits better.
units.anchor: If allowing use of text-generating tools, require citations as you would for any source.

units.why: "Have discussions with your students about the use of AI" is about communicating expectations; no type covers discussion specifically and P09 (stating AI expectations to students) is the closest.
units.anchor: Have discussions with your students about the use of AI
units.policy: Instructors have discussions with students about the use of AI text/answer/product generating tools.

units.why: "Set clear guidelines and expectations - explain why you have these guidelines" asks instructors to state and justify their AI expectations, fitting P09.
units.anchor: Set clear guidelines and expectations
units.policy: Instructors set clear guidelines and expectations and explain why they have these guidelines.

units.why: "Include your specific guidelines in course syllabi and assignment instructions" is a syllabus-statement expectation (P09), phrased as should rather than a mandate.
units.anchor: Include your specific guidelines in course syllabi and assignment instructions.

units.why: "Provide resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing and summarizing, and citation" is instructor support for source skills; it is not a disclosure rule and matches no listed type.
units.anchor: Provide resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing and summarizing, and citation.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors provide resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing, summarizing and citation as an integrity-promoting teaching practice.

units.why: "Have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing" with emphasis on understanding is a teaching practice to prevent misuse; no type covers instructional practice of this kind.
units.anchor: Have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing
units.uncovered_note: Instructors have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing with emphasis on understanding and explaining content rather than rewording.

units.why: "Discuss the purpose of course assignments" is about explaining why work matters, a communication step; it names no AI rule, so the closest type is P09 (communicating expectations).
units.anchor: Discuss the purpose of course assignments.

units.why: "Generate output for your assignments to use as comparison to student work" uses AI output as evidence to identify unauthorized use, matching P40.
units.anchor: Generate output for your assignments to use as comparison to student work.
units.frag_start: Use the tools yourself to understand
units.policy: Instructors use the tools themselves to understand how they work and what they generate, and generate output for their assignments to use as comparison to student work.

units.why: "Review sources (some AI tools fabricate sources)" is a detection step based on checking for fabricated references, i.e. using evidence to identify misuse (P40).
units.anchor: Review sources (some AI tools fabricate sources).

units.why: "follow-up on with students in a conversation" tells instructors to talk with students about specific content before escalating, fitting P57.
units.anchor: follow-up on with students in a conversation
units.policy: Instructors select specific sources, content or choices to follow up on with students in a conversation.

units.why: Detection programs are "not well-tested and may not be accurate", stating that AI detectors are unreliable, so P39 applies.
units.anchor: they are not well-tested and may not be accurate.
units.policy: Online "AI Detection" programs exist, but they are not well-tested and may not be accurate.

units.why: "If you suspect Academic Dishonesty ... contact" the Assistant Director for Academic Integrity routes suspected misuse to the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: If you suspect Academic Dishonesty or have questions about whether an issue
units.policy: Instructors who suspect academic dishonesty or have questions about whether an issue can or should be reported through the Academic Integrity process contact the Assistant Director for Academic Integrity.

units.why: The page notes the Howe Center for Writing Excellence and the Center for Teaching Excellence publish AI resources for teaching and assignment design, which is faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: have published information and resources about AI tools
units.policy: The Howe Center for Writing Excellence and the Center for Teaching Excellence have published information and resources about AI tools as they pertain to teaching and assignment design.

documents.unit: Department of Computer Science and Software Engineering
documents.title: CSE Academic Integrity Guidelines
documents.stance_why: Generative AI is acceptable only "within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor" and unacceptable "when not explicitly approved", i.e. banned unless explicitly permitted, so restrict.
documents.summary: The department's integrity page lists generative AI use as acceptable only within limits the instructor sets for each assignment. Use that fails those requirements or is not explicitly approved is listed as unacceptable.

units.why: The department lists generative AI use "within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor" as acceptable; permission depends on the instructor per assignment, so P04 rather than P02.
units.anchor: within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Use of Generative AI tools such
units.policy: Use of Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Bing, Bard, DALL-E, GitHub Copilot, etc. is acceptable within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor for the individual assignment.

units.why: Listed as unacceptable: using AI "when not explicitly approved by the course instructor", a fallback that unapproved use is banned (P06); I chose P06 over P36 because the passage defines the default, not the sanction.
units.anchor: using Generative AI tools when not explicitly approved by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Use of Generative AI tools such
units.policy: Using Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Bing, Bard, DALL-E, GitHub Copilot, etc. when not explicitly approved by the course instructor is unacceptable.

units.why: The same bullet bars use "without meeting the explicit requirements set forth by the course instructor", so conditions an instructor sets are binding; this is about complying with per-assignment instructor conditions, P04, not the silent-syllabus fallback.
units.anchor: without meeting the explicit requirements set forth by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Use of Generative AI tools such
units.policy: Use of Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Bing, Bard, DALL-E, GitHub Copilot, etc without meeting the explicit requirements set forth by the course instructor is unacceptable.

notes: Computing document has only two AI bullets inside a longer integrity page; non-AI collaboration rules skipped. Two units in miami-u1 are UNCOVERED (instructor teaching practice on source use and paraphrasing). The miami-c1 unacceptable bullet is split into two units (fallback clause and conditions clause).
